candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the pediatric age contraindication for promethazine.

options.A: Administer the medication because promethazine is safer in children under 2 years.
options.B: Hold the medication and clarify the order because promethazine must not be used in children younger than 2 years.
options.C: Give a double dose because young children clear the medication rapidly.
options.D: Administer it only if the child has no fever.

candidate.rationale: Promethazine is contraindicated in pediatric patients younger than 2 years because postmarketing cases of respiratory depression, including fatalities, have occurred in this age group. The nurse should not administer the medication and should clarify the prescription.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Promethazine must not be used in children younger than 2 years because of potentially fatal respiratory depression.
candidate.source_locator: Boxed Warning / Contraindications—Pediatric patients younger than 2 years; risk of fatal respiratory depression
candidate.stem: A provider prescribes promethazine for an 18-month-old child. What should the nurse do?
